newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish KPW approves wood firm Grajewo public issue.
newsitem.headline: Polish KPW approves wood firm Grajewo public issue.

text.p: The Polish Securities Commission (KPW) on Thursday approved trading in wood panel producer Grajewo SA, which is planning a public offer in December and seeking a listing on the bourse's main board.
"Grajewo shares have been approved for public trade," KPW head Jacek Socha told reporters after the commission approved a new issue of 550,000 shares and 2,110,000 existing shares for public trade.
Large investors can register for all of the 260,000 shares in the large-investor tranche on December 12 and December 13.
The small-investor issue of 90,000 shares will take place from December 9 to December 13, while a closed tranche of 200,000 shares will be offered to shareholders 21 days before the issue.
The firm's main shareholders are National Investment Fund No. 15 in Poland's mass privatisation programme, with 33 percent and the state treasury, with 25 percent.
Grajewo President Jan Kowalski said the firm would use the proceeds to help pay debts and continue investments.
The firm plans to invest 54.6 million zlotys this year and 100.9 million zlotys next year, in part from bank loans, after having invested 30.9 million zlotys from 1990 to 1995.
Grajewo made a net profit of 12.4 million zlotys last year on sales of 195.7 million zlotys. It expects to earn 18.5 million zlotys this year on sales of 231.4 million zlotys.
